title: Impacts of tourism on places
log: 2026-11-12T12:44:18Z match: Claude Haiku 5.5 found no bank point the same, so it is written new
2026-11-12T15:15:42Z write: the API refused it in the chapter request, so it is written on its own next

match.reason: The closest bank point, geo-impacts-tourism, covers the benefits and the crowding, environmental and cultural impacts, but it does not teach the brief's management responses (limits on visitor numbers and ecotourism), so adding that would be a new idea rather than a small change.

draft.title: Impacts of tourism on places
card: Tourism brings income and jobs to a place. Visitors spend money on hotels, food, tours and shops, and local people are paid to supply them.

Tourism can also cause problems. Places can become crowded, environments such as reefs and tracks can be damaged, and local prices for housing and food can rise. Local culture can also change as it is shaped to suit visitors.
Some places set a cap on visitor numbers, such as a daily limit on entry permits. This reduces crowding and wear on the environment.
Ecotourism is travel that aims to protect the natural environment and support local people. Visitors are guided in small groups and money goes to conservation or the community.
draft.remember: Tourism can bring income and jobs but may also cause crowding, damage and rising prices. Visitor limits and ecotourism help manage this.

a.q: A small coastal town fills with holiday renters each summer. Local workers can no longer afford rent. Which impact of tourism is this?
a.why: The problem is that rent costs more than local workers can pay, so it is a rise in local prices. Crowding is about too many people in a space, which is not what the town's workers are facing here.
a.clue: Focus on what workers can no longer afford.

b.q: Rangers on a popular island track allow only 100 walkers a day, and each walker needs a permit. Which aim does this limit mainly serve?
opts: Reducing crowding and wear on the track
Raising the price of local housing
Making visitors spend more in the shops
Changing local culture to suit visitors
b.why: A daily cap on walkers keeps numbers down, so the track is less crowded and less worn. It does not lift housing prices, and the card says culture and prices are among the costs that tourism can cause, not things a limit aims to produce.
b.clue: Think about what a cap on numbers does to a track.

b.best: Reducing crowding and wear on the track
